question: According to the WHO definition adopted in India, a stillbirth is defined as the birth of a baby showing no signs of life at or after 28 completed weeks of gestation (or weighing 1,000 g or more), whereas a baby born before 28 weeks showing no signs of life is classified as an abortion.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. The WHO stillbirth threshold is 28 completed weeks (or 1,000 g). Before 28 weeks, loss of the fetus is classified as abortion. This threshold is critical for accurate vital statistics reporting.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The 28-week / 1,000 g threshold is the WHO and Indian standard. Babies born without signs of life before this threshold are classified under the abortion definition, not stillbirth — a distinction that directly affects how perinatal mortality statistics are compiled.
